summary: This RFC defines an extra header field for Abuse Reporting Format reports so the source port of the connection involved in an abuse incident can be identified. It updates RFC 6591.

eli5.summary: Sometimes the address is not enough, so this adds the door number to the complaint.

questions: how to include source port in arf reports
what is the arf source port field
why do arf reports need a source port
subtitle: A new ARF header field that names the source port, so an abuse report can pinpoint who sent the mail.

tldr.problem: Abuse reports carry the source IP address, but when many users share one IP address the address alone cannot identify the origin of the abuse.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a Source-Port field for Abuse Reporting Format reports. It holds the client port of the TCP connection that matches the Source-IP field.
tldr.outcome: Together, the Source-IP and Source-Port fields describe the origin of the abuse completely. It updates RFC 6591.

today: RFC 6692 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6591. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why a Source Port Is Needed
sections.content:
The Abuse Reporting Format (ARF) is an extensible message format for email feedback reports, which report incidents of email abuse. RFC 6591 extended it to report email authentication failures. Both let a report include the source IP address.

The RFC explains, citing another document, that IP address sharing techniques are now deployed. When many clients share an address, the source port values must be in the report if the origin of the abuse is to be identified unambiguously.
sections.eli5: If lots of kids share one house address, a letter to that address does not say which kid did it. The door number inside the house tells you.

sections.title: The Source-Port Field
sections.content:
A new ARF header field called Source-Port is defined. When present, it MUST contain the client port of the TCP connection from which the reported message originated. This is the same connection whose client address is in the Source-IP field.

Generators SHOULD include the field in any report that has a Source-IP field, unless the port number is unavailable. Its use is RECOMMENDED for authentication failure reports generated under RFC 6591.

The formal syntax allows optional comments or folding white space around one to five digits.
sections.eli5: The new line in the complaint says which door number the message came from, matching the street address already written there.

sections.title: Clock Accuracy and IANA
sections.content:
Source ports can be recycled very quickly in Internet Service Provider environments, so accurate clocks matter when reports include port information. A report generator that includes an Arrival-Date field MAY express it in UTC to make it easier to match against local records.

IANA added Source-Port to the "Feedback Report Header Fields" registry. It may appear only once per report and can be related to any Feedback-Type.
sections.eli5: Door numbers get handed to new visitors fast, so you need to know exactly what time the message came. Then you can match it to the right visitor.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The extension introduces no new security considerations beyond those already covered in the base ARF specification. Some considerations about logging source ports in general can be found in the logging recommendations document the RFC cites.
sections.eli5: Adding a door number does not open any new doors for bad guys.

Fontana, H., "Authentication Failure Reporting Using the Abuse Reporting Format", RFC 6591, April 2012.
